method: Size from base rate: median |reaction| scaled by 20d realised vol. Direction only from (a) sign persistence in the last two reactions, (b) run-up asymmetry as a proxy for what is priced, (c) same-week sector read-across. Legible narrative is discounted as priced. key_drivers: Sector-wide AI-infrastructure de-rating still unfolding into the print; Nasdaq 100 in correction
Last two earnings reactions both negative (-9.2%, -7.2%)
Down 23.8% over 20 days; 07-20 bounce explicitly described as technical, not catalyst-driven
Beta 5.5, 86% realised vol - reaction size will exceed the 6.5% median
Bull case (45% revenue growth, 9x colocation) is legible and already published
what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the July de-rating had already fully repriced contracted HPC colocation revenue, making an in-line print a relief event.
reasoning: Regime dominates. A high-beta, unprofitable AI-infra name prints into an active sector unwind with two consecutive negative reactions behind it. Oversold conditions argue for relief, but the only pre-print evidence calls the recent bounce technical. Direction edge is thin; size conviction is high - expect roughly 1.5x the 6.5% median given 86% vol.

what_would_change_my_mind: A credit-quality surprise or reserve build, which is the only thing that historically moves a bank like this more than two percent.

what_would_change_my_mind: Backlog or book-to-bill deceleration that ties Quanta's order book to the data-center capex being repriced, rather than to utility grid spend.
reasoning: Run-up asymmetry and reaction history point the same way, which is my threshold for leaving Neutral. The Comfort Systems read-across cuts against and keeps this a lean, not a strong call. Size well above the 3.85% median.
